- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 3–5% from recent high), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 7–10 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing direction 1–2 days ahead.
